title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 319–320). Π = Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}: free on l_0, l_1, with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1 up to ordering convention. Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a profinite group generated by an involution σ_∞ (with conjugates σ_0, σ_1) and an element ρ of order 3. The relations ε_0 = σ_∞ρ with ε_0^2 = l_0, and ε_1 = ρσ_∞ = σ_0ρ with ε_1^2 = l_1, make it look like (Z/2 * Z/3)^ ≅ PSL_2(Z)^, the orbifold π_1 of the j-line P^1(2,3,∞). In that reading Π sits inside it like Γ(2) (index 6): ε_0 is the parabolic T and l_0 = T^2. This identification is my reading; it is not stated on the page.

On top of that inclusion there is a second map, the homomorphism φ̂ of (18): l_0 ↦ ε_0, l_1 ↦ σ_∞, l_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}. One has ρ^{-1}·σ_∞·σ_∞ρ = 1, so φ̂ is the surjection onto the orbifold group. It kills l_1^2 and l_∞^3, i.e. it comes from the open orbifold immersion P^1−{0,1,∞} ⊂ P^1(·,2,3).

The outer action u on Π is of Galois / GT type: u(l_0) is conjugate to l_0^ρ (ρ ∈ Ẑ^* the cyclotomic exponent) via g_0, and g_1 = σ_∞(g_0). It is assumed to come from an effective action commuting with σ_∞, which also acts on Ŝ^+.

The question: does φ̂ commute with u up to an inner automorphism? Concretely, is there λ with φ̂(ux) = λ u(φ̂x) λ^{-1}?

Step 1 (p. 319, x = l_0). This forces λ = φ̂(g_0) ε_0^{-β} g_0^{-1} for some β ∈ Ẑ.

Step 2 (this page, x = l_1), giving (23).
- l'_1 = σ_∞, and σ_∞^ρ = σ_∞ because ρ is a unit, hence odd (the margin's '(Z/2Z)^* = 1').
- u fixes σ_∞, so the condition is that λ^{-1}φ̂(g_1) centralizes σ_∞.
- Using (22), λ^{-1}φ̂(g_1) = g_0 ε_0^β φ̂(h_0^{-1}), with h_0^{-1} = g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0).
- Pass to the inverse and conjugate by σ_∞. Use σ_∞ ε_0 σ_∞ = ε_1 and σ_∞(g_0)^{-1}g_0 = h_0.
- This gives the boxed condition (24): ε_1^{-β} h_0 ε_0^{β} = σ_∞(φ̂(h_0))^{-1} φ̂(h_0).

Rewriting. With the 'twisted commutator' μ~ = σ_∞(μ)^{-1}μ = [σ_∞, μ], one has h_0 = g_0~, and (24) becomes (27): ε_1^{-β} g_0~ ε_0^{β} = (φ̂(g_0~))~.

Note that (24) mixes g_0 seen through the inclusion Γ(2) ⊂ PSL_2 and through the surjection φ̂.

Margins.
- Left NB: changing g_0 to g_0 l_0^λ changes h_0 to l_1^{-λ} h_0 l_0^{λ} = ε_1^{-2λ} h_0 ε_0^{2λ}, so β becomes β − 2λ. Grothendieck suggests β can be normalized to its parity ('pair ou impair'), but writes 'Comment ?', showing doubt.
- Right NB / (24 bis): λ can be rewritten as φ̂(σ_∞(g_0)), as anticipated on p. 319.

The next page states the result as a Proposition. φ̂ commutes with the given outer action iff some β ∈ Ẑ satisfies (24)/(27); for fixed β this is equivalent to the l_∞ condition (28).
errors: In (23) the exponent should be the cyclotomic unit ρ (ℓ'_1^ρ), not β. The image reads 'ρ', and the margin argument σ_∞^ρ = σ_∞ uses that ρ ∈ Ẑ^* is odd.

The NB on normalizing β is incomplete, as Grothendieck himself flags ('Comment ?'). Changing g_0 to g_0 l_0^λ also changes φ̂(h_0) and hence the right side of (24). So the claim that only the parity of β matters is not justified on the page.
The step λ^{-1}φ̂(g_1) = g_0 ε_0^β φ̂(g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0)) silently uses φ̂(σ_∞(g_0)) = φ̂(g_1), i.e. compatibility of φ̂ with σ_∞ as applied. This is plausible from the setup but not stated here.

ideas.what: Compatibility of a GT/Galois-type outer action on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with the orbifold surjection onto (Z/2*Z/3)^ (j-line orbifold), reduced to a single equation (24)/(27) with an auxiliary β ∈ Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: Descent of the GT (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) action to PSL_2(Z)^ / π_1^orb(M_{1,1}); 2- and 3-cycle type relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of M_{1,1} and the orders 2,3 relations; this computation itself appears only in these notes

ideas.what: Twisted-commutator operator μ~ = [σ_∞, μ] used to rewrite the compatibility condition
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary / twisted commutator for the involution (cocycle condition for σ_∞-equivariance)

ideas.what: Square-root elements ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, ε_1 = ρσ_∞ with ε_i^2 = l_i, relating the Γ(2)-inclusion and the orbifold surjection

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests that the auxiliary exponent β in the compatibility criterion is determined only modulo 2 by renormalizing g_0, making its parity a basic invariant. He doubts the argument himself ('Comment ?') and does not settle it.
missed.quote: Ceci suggère que, quitte à remplacer g_0 par g_0 ε_0^λ, on peut supposer β ∈ {0,1} (i.e. β "pair ou impair")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small invariant attached to lifting GT/Galois actions from M_{0,4} to the j-line orbifold. It could be checked against known descriptions of the GT action on PSL_2(Z)^ (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura), but it is likely subsumed by them.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially routine computation of the condition for a GT-type action to descend along P^1−{0,1,∞} → the (2,3,∞) orbifold. The topic (the genus 0 / M_{1,1} link with the orders 2 and 3) is well developed in the GT literature. The only loose end is the unresolved parity question for β, which is minor.
transcription_corrections: (23): read u(ℓ'_1) = int(λ^{-1}φ̂(g_1))(ℓ'_1^ρ), with exponent ρ rather than β.
Top-left margin: likely 'Or σ_∞^ρ = σ_∞ car σ_∞^2 = 1 et ρ ∈ Ẑ^* → (Z/2Z)^* = 1 !' rather than '(Ẑ∧Ẑ)^*'.
'on a encore σ_∞ commutant' should mean that λ^{-1}φ̂(g_1) commutes with σ_∞; 'on a encore à l'inverse' is likely 'ou encore (passant) à l'inverse'.
Left NB: likely g_0' = g_0 l_0^λ (or g_0 ε_0^{2λ}), so that h_0' = ε_1^{-2λ} h_0 ε_0^{2λ} and β' = β − 2λ; the digit after β is hard to read (2 or 3).
Line under the third displayed equation: the braces label σ_∞(g_0ε_0^β)^{-1}(g_0ε_0^β), i.e. the twisted commutator of g_0 ε_0^β.
